index_convention: native zero-based traceEvents index; not Perfetto slice id
selection: All kernel GPU events whose correlated cuda_runtime/cuda_driver launch is nested in the same compiled graph, on its host thread. No kernel-name prefilter.
source_evidence: torchtitan/ops/float8/cuda_gemm.py:201-232: dgrad GEMM, FP8 transpose, then wgrad GEMM and unpad
torchtitan/models/common/norms/cute_gated_norm/backward.py:1320-1365: WFin completes dgate_down,dgate_up,dweight; separate dx kernel
torchtitan/models/common/ffn/__init__.py:104-121: w1/w3 then fused SwiGLU then w2
limitations: Trace has no tensor shapes or generated FX/Inductor code; individual BF16 GEMM-to-weight and w1-versus-w3 labels are inferred, not directly recorded.

Producer completion denotes a local BF16 gradient value. The current FP32 reduce-scatter buffer is populated later by whole-group packing. Early reduce-scatter needs chunk conversion/packing, ordering, lifetime protection and readiness across all ranks.
The GFSDP completion hook is attached to module inputs. A last weight-gradient kernel is not automatically the module-hook boundary: returned input gradients and any branch sum must also complete.

Ordinal 97 is a fused add/norm-preparation kernel consistent with the FFN input-gradient join. Its exact operands are unrecorded. The boundary after it is a conservative candidate, not a measured hook in a separately compiled FFN.
Norm WFin finalizes parameter outputs in source-defined gradient dtypes. The adjacent copy may convert a parameter gradient or an input gradient; its output identity is unresolved.
Remaining kernel activity is the union of all later kernels in this MTP compiled graph; it is an overlap opportunity ceiling, not measured overlap, communication duration, or saved step time.
Changing callable, compilation, GFSDP or activation-checkpoint boundaries can change fusion, recomputation and kernel order. Existing timing does not predict the changed execution exactly.
No GPU execution or training-source modifications were performed.

integration_findings.current_grouping: The full MTP layer is one non-MoE GFSDP unit and one fullgraph compiled block; communication starts after its complete backward returns.
integration_findings.largest_early_group: FFN w1/w2/w3: 513 MiB of FP32 reduction input, approximately 57.4 percent of the 893.674 MiB MTP group.
integration_findings.recommended_first_boundary: Expose the FFN as a callable/compiled/GFSDP completion unit and measure reduce-scatter of its gradients while the remaining MTP backward executes.
integration_findings.finer_boundary: FFN w2: 171 MiB becomes locally available earlier, with approximately 12.1-12.4 ms remaining elapsed MTP work; exploiting it requires an additional operator/module completion boundary.
integration_findings.not_sufficient: Splitting parameter lists under the unchanged opaque MTP compiled backward does not establish an early gradient completion hook.
integration_findings.communication_availability: In all three microbatches, stream 24 has completed the preceding head collective and norm-weight all-gather before the candidate whole-FFN boundary.
integration_findings.required_runtime_evidence: All-rank readiness and collective ordering; actual FP32 packing and chunk reduce-scatter durations; overlap under contention; numerical parity and repeated unprofiled throughput.
integration_findings.independent_review: Reviewed producer-vs-input-hook readiness, FP8 gradient roles, BF16 mapping ambiguity, and the distinction between overlap windows and speedup.
